question: How did a 1944 lawsuit by a film actress end the studios' power to keep stars under contract indefinitely?
answer: By counting calendar years. Warner Bros. added every suspension, imposed when Olivia de Havilland refused a part, to the end of her seven-year contract. A California appeals court ruled that seven years meant seven calendar years. Record labels won a partial carve-out in 1987 and can still sue artists for undelivered albums.
move: Read a contract's clock: who can stop it, and who can restart it.
source: De Havilland v. Warner Bros. Pictures, 1944
reference: De Havilland v. Warner Bros. Pictures, 67 Cal. App. 2d 225, California Court of Appeal, 1944
